newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: "Adult" soft drinks win 35 pct of Australia market.
newsitem.headline: "Adult" soft drinks win 35 pct of Australia market.

text.p: Older, health-conscious soft drink lovers are driving a A$385 million "adult-rated" soft drink market in Australia which has taken the industry by surprise, according to a study released on Thursday.
The market now makes up 35 percent of Australia's A$1.1 billion non-cola soft drink market, the study by research group Mintel Australia said.
Growth has come from older consumers, mainly women, who still want traditional carbonated beverages, but prefer less sweet drinks and want less additives and sugar.
Mintel listed adult-rated soft drinks as diet non-colas, mixers such as bitter lemon, mineral waters and other beverages such as lemon, lime and bitters drinks.
Some of the products included old favourites, but the category has also been expanded with the introduction of new drinks, such as grape flavours and herbal soft drinks, it said.
Of those drinking the adult beverages, 65 percent were over the age of 35 and 59 percent were women, the study found.
This compared with other non-cola soft drinks, were only 42 percent of consumers were over the age of 35 and only 45 percent were female.
Mintel said the emergence of the new market mirrored developments overseas and represented a substantial growth opportunity given the ageing of the Australian population.
Beverage companies overseas are already developing or re-positioning products with the new target audience in mind, it said.
